thread:
aria_sec: FYI saw a ~1.4k spike in TLS handshake rejects from eu-north -> svc-notify starting 2026-05-12T04:00Z. Error looks like client cert CN=svc-notify-old

ben_sre: sample ingress log:
`2026-05-12T04:02:11Z ingress-eun svc-notify="svc-notify-01" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-notify-old, expected svc-notify)`

kai_infra: We ran RBAC regrouping last week to move keystore ownership to group infra-ops. Ill check KMS audit.

rotator-bot: rotator: rotation job keystore-notify-eun-20260512-01 completed at 2026-05-12T03:58:00Z using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

ben_sre: KMS audit around rotation shows decrypts by svc-notify-old and rotator-sa:
`{"timestamp":"2026-05-12T03:57:59Z","principal":"svc-notify-old@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt"}`
`{"timestamp":"2026-05-12T03:58:01Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt"}`

aria_sec: So legacy SA still had access and minted certs during rollout. Root cause likely leftover project-level IAM binding after RBAC change.

sam_devex: Mitigation plan: 1) kai remove legacy binding, 2) run canary rotation with rotator-sa, 3) run quick TLS CN verification from eu-north probe, 4) add alert for any KMS decrypt by principals outside allowed list.

kai_infra: Removing binding now and will reconcile terraform state afterwards.

rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation keystore-notify-eun-20260512-02 started at 2026-05-12T04:12:00Z using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

kai_infra: Legacy IAM binding removed @2026-05-12T04:13:25Z. Verified policy no longer lists svc-notify-old.

rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-05-12T04:14:40Z. Issued certs with CN=svc-notify.

ben_sre: Probe `openssl s_client -connect svc-notify.eun.internal:443` shows handshake succeeded and server accepted client cert CN=svc-notify. Reject rate returned to baseline by 04:16Z.

sam_devex: Follow-ups: kai to remove orphan terraform state entry and open PR to add an IAM parity test; sec to add KMS-decrypt alert and weekly decrypt summary; dev to propose rotator pre-check that fails if unexpected principals can decrypt.

aria_sec: Filing incident P2 with root cause = leftover IAM binding after RBAC consolidation; contributing factor = no alerting on unexpected KMS decrypt principals. Thanks team :thumbsup:
